font_deduper.py.summary: Find fonts that share the same PostScript name and keep only one copy.
details: Groups the ``.ttf``/``.woff``/``.woff2`` files below the current directory by the PostScript name read from their ``name`` table with fontTools and reports (or with ``DRY_RUN = False`` deletes) the duplicates.

forfin.py.summary: Run a CLI tool over every file of one extension in the current directory.
details: The first argument is the extension to match, the second the command to execute; the remaining arguments are passed through before the file path. Files are processed in a process pool (75% of the cores) and a success/failure summary is printed, e.g. ``svgo`` for ``.svg`` files.

frmc.py.summary: Strip comments from configuration, shell and make-style files in place.
details: Walks the tree, picks the files whose name or extension is in the allow-list (``Makefile``, ``Dockerfile``, ``.env*``, ``.ini``, ``.conf``, ``requirements.txt``, shell dialects ...) and removes the full-line comments while leaving shebangs, ``#!`` lines and code-only ``#`` characters untouched. Python, YAML and other languages are skipped.

fssim.py.summary: Group similar files by fuzzy hashing (ssdeep / ppdeep).
details: Hashes every file, compares the digests by similarity score and prints the groups (optionally as a table), writing a report, a similarity matrix and a CSRF-free copy of the groups when asked. Useful for spotting near-duplicate documents or binaries.

ftak.py.summary: List functions and classes that contain nothing but a docstring.
details: Parses every ``.py`` file below the current directory and prints ``file:line: kind name`` for each definition whose body is a single string literal, i.e. a placeholder that was never implemented.

funclass_names.py.summary: Rank the function and class names used in a tree by how often they are referenced.
details: Scans Python sources, wheels and tarballs (including ``.tar.zst``), collects the defined functions/classes and every name or attribute use, and writes ``func.json`` and ``class.json`` sorted by usage count. Generic names such as ``main`` or ``run`` are ignored.

fv.py.summary: Page through a text file with :mod:`pydoc`'s pager.
details: A minimal ``less`` replacement: reads the file and hands it to ``pydoc.pager``, which uses the terminal pager and keeps the raw text (no rendering).

gagc.py.summary: Commit the current directory and push it to GitHub with one command.
details: Initializes a repository when needed, updates submodules, stages everything, commits with an ``Auto-commit: <timestamp>`` message and then pushes to the existing ``origin`` — creating a new public GitHub repository with ``gh repo create`` or forking the upstream when the current user does not own it.

gdetect_dup_objects.py.summary: Detect duplicate top-level objects across Python files, ignoring annotations and formatting.
details: Canonicalizes each function, class and constant (annotations stripped, docstrings and whitespace normalised), hashes it and prints the objects that appear in more than one file. Works on the files below the current directory and uses a process pool for the parsing.

generate_unified.py.summary: Bundle the scripts of each folder into one generated dispatcher module.
details: For every top-level folder the ``.py`` files are embedded as source constants in ``<folder>.py`` together with a ``...Unified`` tool class that exposes each script as a subcommand (``info`` lists them). The generated module is compiled and checked for missing annotations before being written and made executable.

get_lic.py.summary: Fetch a license text for an author and year and cache the answer.
details: Looks the license kind up in the local cache (``~/.license``), validates the author and year, inserts them into the template fetched with ``gh api`` and prints the result. Driven by :mod:`click` options ``--author``, ``--year`` (default: this year) and ``--kind``.

get_req.py.summary: Print the ``Requires-Dist`` entries of an installed package, or dump them all.
details: With a package name the declared dependencies are printed one per line; without arguments every installed distribution is read and the mapping is written to ``requirements.json``.

getenc.py.summary: Report the encoding of the files below the current directory as detected by several tools.
details: Cross-checks the BOM, ``tokenize``, chardet, charset_normalizer, cchardet, UnicodeDammit, libmagic and ``ced`` guesses (each used only when installed) and prints the results per file, so the common encoding of a tree can be established.

getpyrepos.py.summary: List the Python repositories of a GitHub user and save them as JSON.
details: Queries the GitHub API for the user's repositories, keeps those written in Python and writes ``<user>_python_repos.json``. Without an argument it walks the currently trending users and writes ``trending_github_python_users.json`` instead.
